data.title: KEC International wins ₹2,872 crore orders from Power Grid, its largest India T&D order
data.description:
KEC International has secured orders worth ₹2,872 crore from Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd (PGCIL) for the design, supply and installation of 765 kV transmission lines, according to a company release filed with the BSE on October 24.

The company said the orders mark the largest-ever single order for its India transmission and distribution (T&D) business. The projects are linked to the evacuation of 8.5 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy from Gujarat.

The orders have significantly expanded KEC International's domestic T&D order book, the company said in the release.

Vimal Kejriwal, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of KEC International, said the company had secured the orders amid strong momentum in its T&D business.

"These prestigious 765 kV projects, associated with the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat, have substantially expanded our India T&D order book," Kejriwal said.

The company remained confident about the growth prospects of India's T&D market, supported by rising energy demand and the country's continued focus on strengthening transmission infrastructure.

With the latest order wins, KEC International's year-to-date order intake has crossed ₹13,500 crore, including around ₹9,500 crore from its T&D business, the release stated.

Mumbai-based KEC International is the flagship company of RPG Group and operates in infrastructure engineering, procurement and construction. Its businesses include power transmission and distribution, civil construction, transportation, renewable energy, oil and gas pipelines, and cables and conductors.

KEC shares closed around 1.5% down at ₹327 apiece on the NSE on Friday, October 23. The stock has shed nearly 56% so far this year.

data.title: Bolsonaro and Lula clash on living costs, corruption in final Brazil election debate
data.description:
Key points:
  • Polls show Bolsonaro and Lula close ahead of Sunday runoff
  • Bolsonaro criticized food prices, Lula defended wage policy

By Andre Romani

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks on Friday in the last presidential debate before Sunday's runoff, as both candidates sought to win over undecided voters amid a tight race.

Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, led Lula in the first round of the election earlier this month, but opinion polls have shown the two candidates about even this week after the gap between them narrowed.

Bolsonaro and Lula repeated their campaign proposals during the over two-hour debate hosted by Globo, Brazil's most-watched TV channel, focusing on themes such as the cost of living, welfare and security, while exchanging allegations of corruption.

Lula, who is seeking his fourth term after winning back the presidency in 2022, has defended his government's above-inflation minimum wage increases and stressed that his administration helped millions of Brazilians to escape hunger.

The president said the younger Bolsonaro "is like students studying for college entrance exams. They can memorize things, but they can't learn." He also said that "in the gated community where Bolsonaro lives, people don't go hungry."

Bolsonaro responded by saying food prices for Brazilians rose during Lula's administration, and he criticized a tax reform approved by the current government, projecting the new rules would raise the tax burden on consumers.

"Lula doesn't even remember the last time he went grocery shopping because he lives in a luxury palace now."

The two candidates mostly limited the discussion to pre-established themes in the first few segments of the debate, toning down the personal attacks that marked the only previous debate in the campaign between the two.

At one point, Bolsonaro apologized to Lula after saying the president gives to Brazilians with one hand but "takes away with nine fingers." Lula lost his left little finger in an accident while working as a lathe operator in a factory.

"I will not accept some rich guy, with a highly questionable political practice, calling me 'nine fingers,'" the incumbent said, demanding a retraction.

"Lula, if I offended you by calling you 'nine fingers,' then I sincerely apologize, I sincerely apologize," Bolsonaro said. But he added: "Will you apologize to Brazilians suffering from insecurity ... in debt?"

The discussion heated up in the last minutes of the debate, when both candidates were allowed to interact without moderation, as Lula and Bolsonaro sought to link each other to the fraud involving lender Banco Master.

Lula pressed Bolsonaro on alleged links to the bank's jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Bolsonaro questioned Lula about accusations involving his son and a pension fraud.

The debate was one of the campaign's final events, as Brazilian electoral law bars the candidates from broadcasting radio and TV campaign advertising starting on Saturday. They can still hold rallies until the final hours of the day.

data.title: DGCA Extends Pilot Rest Rule Deadline to March
data.description:
As Airline Face cost pressures... Arindam Majumder New Delhi: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) extended the deadline for the full implementation of revised pilot rest rules by five months to March 31, 2027, as airlines grapple with rising operating costs and concerns over the impact of the guidelines on crew availability, people aware of the matter said.

The latest extension granted earlier this week was the third. The previous relaxation followed IndiGo's operational crisis last December, when India's largest airline cancelled thousands of flights amid a crew shortage. The revised Flight Duty Time Limitations rules, notified early last year, revised the definition of night duty to extend the period covered by an hour, from midnight to 6 am instead of midnight to 5 am.

They also capped the number of landings a pilot can undertake during this period at two and limited duty to 10 hours. In December, the DGCA allowed airlines to operate with three landings when a pilot's duty fell between midnight and 1:55 am or between 5 am and 6 am. Airlines were required to provide rest equivalent to twice the duty period for such operations.

The relaxations, due to expire on October 31, will now continue until March 31. Associations of pilots have opposed such repeated extensions, arguing that they undermine the objective of the revised safety regulations. "Airlines had raised concerns about implementing these rules when the cost structure is already high due to high fuel costs.

They have slowed down hiring of pilots. As a regulator, the DGCA has to take into consideration safety and viable operations," a government official said, adding that no further exemptions would be granted after March 31. The Federation of Indian Airlines, whose members include IndiGo, Air India and SpiceJet, said that the revised rules could increase their pilot requirements by 25%. Airlines also cited high aviation turbine fuel prices, airspace restrictions, additional crew expenses and rupee depreciation as pressures on their finances.

The Federation of Indian Pilots, meanwhile, urged the government to withdraw the relaxations, saying that the regulator was normalising exceptional arrangements rather than forcing airlines to comply with laws. "The five-month extension risked prolonging arrangements intended to address temporary operational difficulties, and gives an impression that mandatory safety requirements may be deferred whenever operational pressures arise," it said in a letter to civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu that ET has seen.

data.title: Airlines Oppose Any Cuts in Slots at Mumbai Airport
data.description:
Forum Gandhi Mumbai: Airlines operating at the Adani Group-controlled Mumbai airport opposed any unilateral reduction or cancellation of flight slots under a proposed traffic reallocation plan for summer 2027, according to letters seen by ET. They asked the airport operator to provide capacity data and details of Terminal 1's redevelopment plan before proceeding with the proposal.

The dispute centres on how the airport will accommodate airlines during the redevelopment of Terminal 1, and whether flight slots will need to be reduced or traffic shifted to manage capacity. At a meeting scheduled for October 28, airlines want Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL), which operates the airport, to provide the actual capacity of the two terminals of the airport, details of the refurbishment timeline and an update on the planned capacity addition at Terminal 2, before decisions are made on the Summer 2027 transition plan.

In a letter on Friday, the Airport Operators Committee (AOC) in Mumbai reiterated that MIAL must comply with the Ministry of Civil Aviation's May 2013 slot-allocation guidelines and the International Air Transport Association's Worldwide Airport Slot Guidelines. Traffic reallocation must not be implemented unilaterally without compliance with the applicable procedures, it said.

The AOC said no substantiated justification was provided for reducing or cancelling slots at the airport, claiming that Terminal 1 was currently handling less than 10 million passengers per annum (MPPA) and that there was an expected capacity addition of 5 MPPA at Terminal 2 by next March. "Any such proposal must be supported by verifiable capacity assessments, operational data and a clear, evidence-based justification," the committee said.

Terminal 1's current capacity is 15 million passengers and the airport operator plans to increase it to 20 million. MIAL earlier this week told airlines that they were free to shift some or all of their operations to the new airport in Navi Mumbai, suspend services until its Terminal 1 reopens in 2030, or pursue other options from summer 2027. The Navi Mumbai airport is also controlled by Adani Airports Holdings.

Meanwhile, the MIAL chief airport officer's office on Friday sent a second reminder to airlines that had not yet held discussions with the airport operator on the transition plan. It asked them to arrange consultations with the airport's network-planning and commercial teams to help finalise the plan ahead of the October 28 stakeholder meeting. In its response, the AOC said airlines supported the T1 refurbishment "as a priority and without any further delay".

data.title: IndusInd Returns to Black in Q2 as Provisions Halve
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: IndusInd Bank reported a consolidated net profit of 1,242 crore at the end of the September quarter against a net loss of 437 crore a year earlier, helped by a sharp decline in provisions, higher fee income and an improvement in asset quality.

The private sector lender's net interest income (NII) rose 4% year-on-year to 4,569 crore at the end of the September quarter from 4,409 crore in the same quarter last year, while other income jumped 36% to 2,248 crore from 1,651 crore. The improvement in profitability was largely driven by a 54% year-on-year decline in provisions and contingencies to 1,223 crore from 2,631 crore, reflecting moderation in credit stress.

Gross slippages, or fresh additions to bad loans, declined 42% during the September quarter to 1,460 crore from 2,537 crore a year earlier. "(The quarter) reflects the growing strength of the franchise and the progress we have made in rebuilding momentum across the bank," Rajiv Anand, MD, IndusInd Bank, said after the earnings. "Growth has strengthened, profitability has improved, asset quality trends remain encouraging, and our funding profile is becoming more granular and resilient." Asset quality improved, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declining 87 basis points to 2.7% from 3.6% a year earlier. The net NPA ratio fell 21 basis points to 0.8% from 1.0%. Despite the improvement in earnings, net interest margins remained under pressure. NIM narrowed by 9 basis points year-on-year to 3.2% from 3.3%, with the bank attributing the pressure to mobilisation of foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits. One basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point.

The bank's loan book expanded 11% year-on-year to 3.6 lakh crore from 3.3 lakh crore. Retail advances rose 13% to 2.1 lakh crore, while wholesale advances increased 10% to 1.5 lakh crore. Within retail lending, consumer banking advances surged 38% to 76,341 crore, although the growth included 16,564 crore of advances linked to FCNR(B) deposits.

Vehicle finance loans grew 5% to 1.0 lakh crore, while rural banking advances contracted 6% to 33,338 crore. The microloan portfolio shrank 18% year-on-year to 17,571 crore from 21,321 crore, reflecting continued contraction in the segment. Credit card receivables declined 15% to 9,167 crore from 10,747 crore. Home loans, however, rose 39% to 7,733 crore. On the liabilities side, deposits grew 10% year-on-year to 4.3 lakh crore from 3.9 lakh crore. Current account deposits increased 15% to 36,742 crore, while savings account deposits declined 5% to 83,024 crore.

data.title: Shriram Fin Q2 Net up 59%
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Shriram Finance, in which Japan's Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) has a significant stake, reported a 59.4% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to 3,677 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, driven by growth in net interest income and lower finance costs.

It reported a net profit of 2,307 crore a year earlier. Net interest margin (NIM), a measure of core profitability, improved to 9.52% from 8.19% a year earlier. "Our long-term guidance has consistently been around 8.5%, but it will take some time to return to that level. For the next two quarters, we expect NIM to remain around 9%," said Parag Sharma, MD & CEO, in an interview with ET. He attributed growth in profit to two factors. "The first was growth in business volumes, and the second was the substantial benefit from lower interest costs, which lifted net interest income," he added.

Net interest income rose 38% to 8,661 crore from 6,267 crore. The increase was driven by a 15.6% rise in interest income to 13,669 crore, while interest expenses fell 9.9% to 5,008 crore. Operating profit increased 53.3% to 6,809 crore, while the cost-to-income ratio improved to 22.52% from 27.76%. Core operating profit, which excludes other income, rose 53.5% to 6,682 crore.

The profit growth came despite a 41% increase in loan losses and provisions to 1,877 crore from 1,333 crore in the year-ago quarter. On a sequential basis, provisions rose 28.3%. Total income increased 15.8% to 13,799 crore, while profit before tax rose 58.6% to 4,932 crore. Net profit was 6.8% higher sequentially than 3,445 crore in the June quarter. Assets under management (AUM) grew 17% year on year and 4.9% sequentially to 3.29 lakh crore at the end of September. The broader vehicle and equipment portfolio stood at 2.61 lakh crore, accounting for 79.46% of total AUM.

data.title: SBI Cards Q2 Profit Jumps 75%
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: SBI Cards and Payment Services reported a 75% year-on-year rise in net profit to 778 crore for the September quarter, driven by a sharp decline in credit costs and an improvement in asset quality, even as corporate card spends contracted and outstanding receivables declined.

The company had reported a net profit of 445 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Total income increased 3% year on year to 5,302 crore from 5,136 crore. Impairment losses and bad debt expenses declined 37% year on year to 819 crore from 1,293 crore, providing a significant boost to profitability.

The company's net interest margin (NIM) narrowed by 42 basis points year on year to 10.8%. "During Q2 of FY27, we continued to focus on building a healthy, sustainable and well-balanced portfolio, while maintaining our priorities around profitable customer acquisition, customer engagement, operating efficiency and portfolio quality," said Salila Pande, MD, SBI Cards, during the post-earnings analyst call.

The company's gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio improved to 1.90% at September-end from 2.85% a year earlier, while the net NPA ratio declined to 0.77% from 1.29%. Gross write-offs fell 34% year on year to 849 crore, reflecting improved credit quality in its portfolio. However, growth in the underlying business remained modest. Overall credit card spends increased just 3% year on year to 1.11 lakh crore from 1.07 lakh crore.

data.title: Pawan Hans Asked to Chart Five-Year Turnaround Plan by This Year End
data.description:
Anuradha Shukla New Delhi: The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) has asked state-owned helicopter operator Pawan Hans to submit a five-year turnaround plan by December, focusing on financial and organisational restructuring, steps to enhance operational and fleet efficiencies, and the identification of new verticals and revenue streams.

The move comes amid the government's push to handhold central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) with strategic potential and improve their performance. The communication, sent in the first week of October, follows a September meeting between the Pawan Hans management and senior DPE officials.

Pawan Hans management is also planning to engage a senior consultant to help prepare the plan, officials said. "There is a lot of potential for the state-owned helicopter operator and, with proper hand-holding, it can grow multifold," a senior official said. The move follows an instruction by a committee headed by cabinet secretary TV Somanathan, which has recommended handholding CPSEs that can be strategic to the medium- to long-term growth of the country.

The roadmap is expected to assess opportunities in heli-tourism, religious tourism, helicopter emergency medical services, regional connectivity and other aviation-related businesses. The development of heliports and services for remote and underserved destinations could feature in the expansion strategy. Pawan Hans has separately been exploring electric seaplane technology. In August, it signed a non-binding MoU with Norway's Noemi Aerospace to explore collaboration in electric seaplanes and sustainable aviation.

The turnaround exercise follows the collapse of an earlier divestment attempt. In May 2022, the government selected a consortium led by Star9 Mobility Pvt Ltd to acquire 51% stake in the company for 211.14 crore. The process was subsequently called off in July 2023 amid pending legal cases. The civil aviation ministry is the administrative ministry for Pawan Hans, while the DPE, under the finance ministry, frames policy guidelines relating to the performance and management of CPSEs.

The ministry has already allocated 450 crore for fleet modernisation, linking the company's expansion plans to the government's push to strengthen indigenous helicopter capacity and improve connectivity to remote regions under the Udaan scheme. The proposed induction of Dhruv helicopters from Hindustan Aeronautics into Pawan Hans is also part of the Centre's effort to strengthen indigenous aviation capabilities.

data.title: Coforge Q2 Net Profit Jumps 56.5% to 588 cr on Encora Deal
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: Mid-size IT services firm Coforge reported a 56.5% year-on-year increase in net profit to 588.1 crore for the second quarter of the fiscal year 2027, aided by a full-quarter contribution from its acquisition of engineering services firm Encora for $2.35 billion.

Sequentially, net profit rose 13.4%. Revenue for the September quarter increased 53.6% year-on-year and 11.6% sequentially to 6,170.8 crore. In dollar terms, revenue stood at $652.2 million, up 10.1% from the preceding quarter on constant currency terms. Contribution from the Encora acquisition was a major reason for the revenue growth this quarter along with large deals. "The demand slowdown that we are talking about is largely on account of the fact that the procurement-driven RFPs have slowed down.

The intensity of the ask around delivering AI-led transformation for enterprises is only getting stronger," chief executive officer Sudhir Singh said in the post-earnings analyst call. and close deals without getting into fistcuffs with other providers around pricing," he added. The second quarter was the first to fully consolidate Encora, since its acquisition in December 2025.

Singh said its margin expansion was ahead of plan and revenue growth should mirror Coforge's from Q3, with the largest deal in Coforge's pipeline involving an Encora client. Encora contributed about $147-$148 million in revenue on a constant-currency basis during the quarter, broadly flat against the preceding quarter's comparable full-quarter revenue, chief financial officer Saurabh Goyal said. Deal wins by total contract value stood at $1.04 billion, compared with $691 million in the preceding quarter and $514 million a year earlier. The three-month period saw the Noida-headquartered firm sign eight large deals. Deal wins by total contract value stood at $1.04

data.title: IndiGo, Akasa Air Extend Saudi Flight Cancellations
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: IndiGo and Akasa Air have extended flight cancellations to Saudi Arabia amid continuing security concerns in the Middle East, with IndiGo keeping its Riyadh services suspended until October 31 and flights to three other Saudi cities cancelled until October 27.

The extensions affect services to Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah, key destinations for Indian travellers and workers.

The disruptions come amid attacks on Saudi targets, raising concerns over the safety of airport operations and prompting airlines to reassess their schedules. In a travel advisory on Friday, IndiGo said flights to and from Riyadh would remain cancelled until October 31 (inclusive), while services to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah would remain suspended until October 27 (inclusive).

The airline said it was monitoring developments and coordinating with the relevant authorities. Affected passengers are being notified through their contact details and have been advised to check their flight status before leaving for the airport. Akasa Air had earlier, on October 18, extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 27. The airline is offering affected passengers a full refund, credited to the original payment source within seven days, or rescheduling without an additional charge.

Air India and Air India Express had also suspended operations to Saudi Arabia amid the security situation. The disruptions follow attacks on Saudi targets earlier this month, including an attack at Riyadh airport that killed an Indian national and injured several others.

data.title: Polish PM Tusk Calls for Deeper Tech, AI and Space Ties with India Deeper Tech Ties in AI, Digital Products, Space
data.description:
attends India-Poland Business Forum in city Our Political Bureau Bengaluru: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk called for stronger technology partnerships between India and Poland, identifying artificial intelligence (AI), digital products and space technology as key areas for collaboration as the two countries seek to deepen their strategic partnership.

Speaking at the India-Poland Business Forum in Bengaluru on Friday, he said companies from both countries could combine research capabilities, technology and capital to develop innovative products and expand their presence in global markets. The Polish PM said he saw an opportunity for partnerships in which companies in both countries could combine their research and development teams, technologies and capital to jointly introduce new digital products to the market.

Tusk said India and Poland had the potential to jointly develop AI systems for manufacturing, automation, diagnostics, data analysis and infrastructure management, while also creating affordable tools for small and medium enterprises. He also called for stronger collaboration between universities and research institutions in machine learning, data analysis and the safe use of AI. The Polish PM highlighted opportunities in the space sector and said companies from both countries were already exploring partnerships in satellite components, earth observation, navigation systems, software development, data analytics and space security.

Calling Bengaluru a global centre for computing, research and innovation, Tusk said the city would play a pivotal role in future India-Poland cooperation. He noted that Poland had transformed itself into a modern industrial economy with strengths in engineering and technology and said the next step was to convert bilateral commitments into concrete joint ventures.

Karnataka Seeks Investments CM DK Shivakumar invited Poland to participate as a partner country at Karnataka's Global Investors Meet (GIM) 2027 and pitched the state as a destination for investments in advanced manufacturing, healthcare, technology and clean energy.

He welcomed TZMO Group's proposed Rs 80 crore investment in the KIADB industrial area at Vemgal in Kolar district. The five-acre facility is expected to create 1,000 jobs and introduce the manufacture of smart adult incontinence products in India. The chief minister also highlighted the proposed Karnataka-Katowice Digital and Gaming Corridor, aimed at fostering collaboration in AI, gaming, deep-tech innovation and startup ecosystems.

He urged Polish firms to explore opportunities in Bengaluru's strengths such as AI, software, gaming, robotics and smart manufacturing, while encouraging greater cooperation in research, education and technology transfer. Pointing to Infosys' long-standing presence in Poland, Shivakumar said it underscored the scope for stronger India-Poland technology ties.

He also identified renewable energy, waste-to-energy projects, wastewater treatment and circular economy solutions as promising areas for future collaboration, while inviting Polish companies to explore opportunities across Karnataka's industrial ecosystem. data.title: JSW Steel Net Jumps 3-Fold to 5,279 cr
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: JSW Steel saw a three-fold year-on-year surge in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter to 5,279 crore, boosted by a 13% year-on-year growth in sales volumes to an all-time high. The country's largest steel-maker by capacity also approved adding another 5 million tonnes of capacity at its facility in Utkal in Odisha for an investment of 16,150 crore.

The company also approved several other projects, including capacity expansion at JSW JFE Steel. It sold 7.46 million tonnes of steel during the quarter, while output was at an all-time high of 7.27 million tonnes. This lifted the revenue from operations higher by 21% on year to 54,486 crore. Adjusted for the deconsolidation of Bhushan Power earlier this year, the topline was 31% higher.

Reported earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization rose 58% on year to 10,120 crore, while adjusted Ebitda was 39% higher year-on-year at 9,941 crore. The adjusted profitability numbers exclude foreign exchange gains or losses on the company's long-term borrowings, net of intercompany receivables.

Adjusted Ebitda margins improved to 18.3% from 17.2% earlier, while the adjusted Ebitda made on each tonne of steel rose 24% on year to 13,329. JSW Steel saw a significant 34% drop in finance costs to 1,602 crore, while depreciation and amortization expenses were down by 14% to 2,200 crore.

The steel-maker reported its earnings during market hours on Friday, and its shares closed at 1,187.00 on the BSE, down 2.6% from the previous close. Its consolidated net debt is down to 44,482 at the end of the September quarter as compared to 46,157 crore at the end of June. Net debt to equity ratio at the end of the quarter stood at 0.39 times, down from 0.42 times at the end of the June quarter, while the net debt to Ebitda ratio stood at 1.28 times, down from 1.46 times. JSW Steel has retained its guidance of spending 22,000-24,000 on capital expenditure this year, and has spent 11,136 crore in the first half of the year, with 6,266 crore spent in the September quarter itself. Apart from adding another 5 million tonne of capacity at Utkal in Odisha, the company will also be setting up a 8-million tonne pellet plant at JVML-Vijayanagar and an additional converter and caster in the JVML phase-II expansion. It will set up an additional strand of caster and a plate processing facility at Dolvi.

data.title: Infosys Guidance Shock may Trip Stock Despite Numbers Bounce
data.description:
Ranjit Shinde ET Intelligence Group: The second quarter revenue and profit numbers of Infosys were more or less in line with analysts expectations. However, evaluating the quarterly performance of the country's second largest IT vendor may not be that easy since the cautious management commentary barely reflects the optimism exuded by the improving top line, resilient margin performance and strong deal momentum.

Despite winning a mega deal during the quarter, it reduced the revenue guidance band for the full year, citing increasing competitive intensity and persistent weakness in some of the business verticals. The stock has gained 16% on the bourses over the past two weeks, helped by steady performance from peers in the September quarter and the absence of any major bad news for the sector.

The company declared the quarterly performance after the market hours on Friday. While the numbers are encouraging, the management commentary and a multi-year low projection for annual top line growth may affect the market sentiment in the short term. Infosys recorded second best sequential revenue growth for the September quarter in reported as well as constant currency terms following HCL Technologies, the third largest software exporter. That helped in maintaining its lead over Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), the largest among them and Wipro, the fourth largest, in terms of trailing 12-month (TTM) growth. Moreover, it bagged a mega transformation deal worth $2 billion, taking the total contract value (TCV) to $5.2 billion for the quarter, the highest since the September 2023 quarter when its TCV reached $7.7 billion. The operating margin (Ebit margin) at 21% remained in the guided band of 20-22% and stayed flat year-on-year while showing a tad 10 basis point weakness sequentially.

A large order win and steady top line and margin performance should have typically resulted in an upward revision in the revenue guidance. On the contrary, the company cut the FY27 guidance to 1-2% growth from the previous guidance of 1.5-3% growth. This was well below the expectations of analysts who had anticipated a more benign cut in the guidance.

data.title: Beyond the stipend: how firms are competing for MBA interns
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- The tussle for MBA (Master of Business Administration) talent is moving well before final placements, with companies rolling out scholarships, housing benefits, leadership sessions and business-critical assignments to attract interns and improve their chances of converting them into full-time hires through pre-placement offers (PPOs). All this is being rolled out in a sluggish job market, since firms prefer to extend a pre-placement offer to students who fit the bill after an internship rather than jostle with competitors during the final placement season a few months later.

"The focus is moving beyond the stipend to creating experiences that allow students to apply their learning to real business challenges and explore potential career pathways," said Pranav Jindal, associate dean, admissions and careers, Indian School of Business (ISB).

The strategy comes as students increasingly prioritise career growth, mentorship and meaningful work over stipend size, and employers are responding with more robust internship experiences and greater access to senior management.

From Adani Group's scholarship-backed programme to Avendus Capital's live deal simulations, firms are turning internships into a crucial recruitment channel and a test of future talent.

"For example, investment banking firms are offering front-end roles, FMCG companies are providing opportunities to work on market launch strategies for new product lines, and conglomerates are bringing structured strategic leadership development programmes," ISB's Jindal said.

Energy-to-airports firm Adani Group has the Adani Academic Leadership Programme (AALP) through which selected interns receive a scholarship that covers the fees for the two-year MBA programme, except for mess fees.

"Adani Group has participated in the final placement process at IIM (Indian Institute of Management) Lucknow in the past. However, following the introduction of the Adani Academic Leadership Programme, the Group has increasingly focused on engaging with students through summer internships, with the potential for pre-placement offers and subsequent full-time employment," said Prem Prakash Dewani, chairperson, placement, IIM Lucknow (IIM-L) in an email response to Mint.

In a pre-placement offer (PPO), the company extends an offer to the student right after the internship. The student has the right to refuse a PPO.

This is the second year of AALP, and fees at some of the older IIMs can range from Rs.20 to Rs.27 lakh.

Interestingly, IIM-L told Mint that the two-year scholarship is extended to all AALP interns, irrespective of whether they receive or accept a PPO. The scholarship is "not contingent on their subsequent placement outcome with the Group".

The Adani Group did not respond to Mint's queries.

ISB typically has 820 students across its Hyderabad and Mohali campuses in its one-year MBA programme. "Startups, meanwhile, are offering founder's office opportunities, where students work closely with co-founders and senior leadership, shadow leaders as they make critical business decisions, and gain exposure to the realities of building and scaling a business," said Jindal of ISB.

Internships at B-schools typically take place in May-June, after which the student may receive a PPO. If the student accepts, she does not have to sit through the final campus placement process, which takes place a few months later. The stipends in the more established B-schools are a couple of lakhs per month.

What is interesting, though, is that these students are no longer on the periphery of workplace activities but are in the thick of things. For the company, an engaged student will lead to a quicker acceptance of a PPO, thereby saving the time and effort of going on the hunt again during final placement season.

While PPOs are coming in for the internships that took place earlier in the year (batch of 2025-27), students from the batch of 2026-28 are gearing up for their internship interviews.

Over the last 2 years, Avendus Capital's investment banking arm has increased its hiring from B-schools via the PPO route to 60% from 38%. For the 2026-2028 batch, Avendus presented a two-hour live deal scenario to the students, who were asked to propose how they would handle the case.

"We realised that students assumed investment banking is a heavy number-crunching job but were unaware of the stakeholder management involved in creating a competitive deal situation towards driving outcomes," said Divya Agarwal, executive director and head, human resources at Avendus Investment Banking. "In one of the deals, the students were surprised that they may have 20 stakeholders in one case," she added.

The case study discussions are when Avendus will zero in on the candidate. "Starting this year, internship interviews will only happen after the deep-dive session."

IIM Indore pointed out that the students are looking for a networking opportunity that gets them closer to how the company and its top deck functions. "They've realized that industry immersion and networking can matter as much as the pay, sometimes more," said Himanshu Rai, director, IIM Indore.

For instance, at IIM Indore, a leading building materials and construction company places its management interns at its manufacturing plants, regardless of their engineering background, so that they understand how the product is actually made.

Companies are wooing students with carrots beyond pay. "The better programmes give interns a lot of what a full-time employee gets. That includes housing arranged or subsidised by the company and help with relocation, so moving to a new city isn't something they have to worry about," said Rai of IIM Indore.

Tyre-to-life sciences business house RPG Group redesigned its summer internship programme to get interns to work on business-critical projects. "Our campus insights showed that students increasingly look beyond just the employer brand: they want clarity on the role, career trajectory, learning opportunities and the probability of converting an internship into a full-time opportunity. Internship experiences also strongly influence peer perception on campus," said an RPG spokesperson.

"The usual 40 minute -1 hour interview format is not effective any more," Narayanan Ramaswamy, partner and national leader of the education and skill development practice at KPMG in India, said. Companies are using internships more and more to spot original thinkers and strong problem-solvers in the artificial intelligence era, he added.

data.title: Robot Consulting Announces Receipt of Nasdaq Delisting Determination and Request to Appeal such Determination Before a Hearings Panel
data.description:
TOKYO, JP / ACCESS Newswire / October 24, 2026 / Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. ("Robot Consulting" or the "Company"), a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions and legal technology, announced it has received a delisting determination from the Listing Qualifications Department (the "Staff") of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") notifying the Company of the Staff's determination to delist the Company's American Depository Shares ("ADSs") pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rules 5101 and IM-5101-4.

The Staff's determination is based on concerns regarding historical trading activity in the Company's securities and Nasdaq's belief that certain factors may have made the Company's securities susceptible to manipulation by third parties.

Nasdaq Listing Rule IM-5101-4 allows Nasdaq "to exercise discretion to delist a company from Nasdaq based on the potential for one or more third parties to engage in misconduct impacting a company's securities where the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission] has implemented a temporary trading suspension." Nasdaq has articulated its belief that the ability for third parties to manipulate a security's price indicates that the security does not have sufficient liquidity to promote fair and orderly markets and, therefore, delisting is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.

The Company has appealed the Staff's determination to a Hearings Panel (the "Panel") on October 23, 2026. As a result of the appeal, the suspension of the Company's securities and the filing of the Form 25-NSE by Nasdaq with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") will be stayed pending the Panel's review and decision, although the existing trading halt will remain in effect unless and until it has been lifted by Nasdaq.

To date, Nasdaq has not claimed or communicated a view that there has been any wrongdoing by the Company, whether in regard to Nasdaq's investigation of the recent trading activity of the Company's securities or otherwise. The delisting determination does not have any immediate effect on the Company's ongoing business operations or financial condition, and the Company will continue to conduct its business in the ordinary course.

About Robot Consulting Co., Ltd.

Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. is a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions with an intention to expand into legal technology. The Company's major product, "Labor Robot," is a cloud-based human resource management system that helps users track employee attendance, manage sales orders, and journalize accounting items. Robot Consulting also assists users with grant and subsidy applications and provides consulting and support services for digital transformation to small and medium-sized businesses. Robot Consulting also aims to create more software and services related to digital transformation and legal technology. The Company has launched "Robot Lawyer," a platform that provides preliminary legal consultation resources to individuals and small businesses, particularly with respect to defamatory online posts or other reputational harm. For more information, visit www.robotconsulting.net.

data.title: Suspect arrested as fire engulfs Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest', German police say
data.description:
German police said they had detained a suspect after fire broke out at a historic mountain guest house known as the "Eagle's Nest", used as a retreat by Nazi officials, including the dictator Adolf Hitler.

Around 200 firefighters and emergency personnel in the area around Berchtesgaden in the southern region of Bavaria were battling the flames after the building, known as the Kehlsteinhaus, caught fire on Friday, police said.

Police are investigating whether the suspect, who was detained close to the scene, was connected to the fire, they said in a statement.

There was no immediate word about a possible motive.

Built in 1938 as a guest house for Nazi officials and their guests, the building, in a spectacular Alpine setting, is separate from Hitler's nearby summer residence, known as the Berghof.

Now owned by the state of Bavaria, the Kehlsteinhaus was classified after the war as a historical monument recalling the Nazi period.

data.title: Wall Street closes lower to end rocky week
data.description:
Wall Street's main ​indexes closed lower on Friday even as technology shares steadied somewhat to end a turbulent week for the market-driving AI trade, ‌and investors looked ahead to a busy slate of corporate earnings and a Federal Reserve interest-rate policy meeting.

The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss a day after the tech-heavy index suffered its biggest one-day drop since June, as concerns flared over financing costs to support heavy AI investment spending. The S&P 500 technology sector posted a 0.35% gain on Friday.

Most ​S&P 500 sectors fell, however, including declines of well over 1% for the consumer staples and consumer discretionary groups as well as the ​financials sector.

Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies report quarterly results, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, three AI hyperscalers whose ⁠capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

"There is still fallout from the questioning of the AI trade," said Kristina Hooper, chief market ​strategist at Man Group. "There's certainly the potential that we see less invested in an AI data center build-out next year than has been projected. So I certainly ​think that's giving pause."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16; the S&P 500 lost 39.75 points, or 0.52%, to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 53.52 points, or 0.21%, to 25,955.34.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%. The blue-chip Dow rose 0.4%, its third straight weekly gain.

Telecommunications stocks fell, ​weighing on the communication services sector, after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier.

Shares of AT&T and ​T-Mobile both sank nearly 8% while Verizon shed 1.2%. SpaceX shares rose 1.9%. US cell tower operators gained, with Crown Castle up 9% and American Tower up 4%.

The energy ‌sector rose ⁠2.5%, hitting a record high. Brent crude hit its highest level since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

American Express shares fell 3.7%, weighing on the Dow. The company raised its profit forecast as it also announced plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce.

SLB shares rose 7% after the oilfield services provider beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit.

Data from the University of Michigan showed US consumer sentiment edged ​down near a record low in ​October, as rising prices because of ⁠the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with robust corporate profit growth underpinning gains for major equity indexes this year. S&P 500 companies are on track to have increased earnings ​by more than 32% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.

The Fed is expected to keep interest ​rates steady when it ⁠gives its policy statement on Wednesday, but investors will be eager for clues about whether the US central bank will hike rates at its December meeting. Wall Street is also increasingly focused on the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.72-to-1 ratio on the New ⁠York Stock ​Exchange. On the Nasdaq, declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.57-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted ​18 new 52-week highs and 8 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 74 new highs and 334 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 15.4 billion shares, compared with the 17.2 billion ​average over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: Azerbaijan sees ties with India moving to "higher levels"
data.description:
Baku, Oct. 23 -- Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov expressed confidence on Friday that bilateral relations with India are progressing towards higher levels, noting expanding prospects across energy sectors, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and logistical corridors, while characterising External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar's official visit to Baku as "a very valuable meeting".

Following his meeting with EAM Jaishankar in the Azerbaijani capital, Bayramov described the exchange as comprehensive, constructive and highly productive, addressing various bilateral, regional and global issues.

Bayramov noted that this diplomatic engagement served as a logical continuation of previous high-level interactions between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit held in Bishkek last month.

Emphasising commercial relations, the top Azerbaijani diplomat stated that bilateral trade volume had reached approximately USD 600 million this year, though he acknowledged that this figure remained below the true economic capacity of both nations. The minister underscored that India's ONGC had enhanced its stake in a major oil and gas project within Azerbaijan, alongside more than 1,000 Indian corporate entities currently active in the country.

Furthermore, Bayramov pointed to energy, agricultural cooperation and pharmaceutical collaboration as key growth areas, alongside major transit networks connecting eastern, western, northern and southern corridors, leveraging Azerbaijan's strategic geographical location.

Concerning cultural and interpersonal connections, Bayramov reported that two direct flight routes operated between Baku and Delhi, approximately 500 Indian scholars had enrolled in Azerbaijani higher education institutions this year, and over 30 Indian cinematic productions had utilised local backdrops in recent years.

The two foreign ministers additionally evaluated geopolitical conditions within the South Caucasus, encompassing peace and normalisation efforts between Armenia and Azerbaijan, escalating frictions in the Middle East and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, according to Bayramov.

"We believe that this visit and the discussions that we have had on the various issues will have a good impact on the development of the bilateral relationship between our two nations," Bayramov stated, according to the English translation of his remarks.

Earlier on Friday, EAM Jaishankar called on Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Baku, where both leaders held detailed discussions aimed at deepening cooperative frameworks between the two countries.

"Pleased to call on Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan in Baku this morning. Conveyed the greetings of President Droupadi Murmu and PM Modi. Discussed strengthening the relationship between our two countries. Appreciate his positive sentiments for this shared endeavour," EAM Jaishankar posted on X.

data.title: Infosys Growth Outlook Sours Despite Strong Deal Wins
data.description:
Revenue growth guidance narrowed to 1 to 2 per cent despite USD 5.2 billion in Q2 deal wins; net profit misses analyst estimates as US-listed shares fall

Infosys cut its FY27 revenue growth forecast on Friday as weakness in its largest market, North America, weighed on its outlook, despite stronger deal bookings. Net profit for the September quarter rose 6.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) but fell short of analyst estimates, while the revised guidance sent its US-listed shares lower in premarket trading.

The Bengaluru-based IT services major lowered its constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1 to 2 per cent for FY27 from 1.5 to 3 per cent previously, signalling continued pressure on near-term growth. The revision came even as large-deal total contract value (TCV) increased to USD 5.2 billion in the quarter from USD 3.1 billion a year earlier, with 62 per cent of the deal value classified as net new business.

North America Weakness Weighs On Outlook

Revenue from North America, which accounts for more than half of Infosys’ sales, declined 1.5 per cent YoY in constant-currency terms in the September quarter, marking the region’s weakest performance in two years. The company cited softer demand, with high-technology and retail clients in the region scaling down projects.

Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said the quarter had been softer, with pricing pressure arising from intense competition and clients seeking to capture productivity gains from artificial intelligence (AI). These factors were reflected in the revised growth guidance, he said during the company’s earnings call.

Deal Bookings Rise As Revenue Outlook Weakens

Infosys reported large-deal TCV of USD 5.2 billion in Q2, up from USD 3.1 billion in the year-ago quarter and USD 3.6 billion in the preceding quarter. Of the total deal value, 62 per cent came from net-new business.

However, the stronger bookings did not prevent Infosys from lowering its full-year growth forecast. Contract wins represent the value of business secured, while the revenue contribution depends on project commencement, execution and the recognition of services over time. The revised guidance points to limited confidence in a stronger near-term growth trajectory, even as the company continues to win large transformation engagements. Infosys retained its FY27 operating-margin guidance at 20 to 22 per cent.

Infosys reported consolidated net profit of Rs 7,823 crore for the September quarter, up 6.2 per cent from Rs 7,364 crore a year earlier. The figure was below the analyst estimates. Revenue rose 10.7 per cent YoY to Rs 49,244 crore. In constant-currency terms, revenue grew 1.5 per cent YoY and 1.2 per cent sequentially, while operating margin remained stable at 21 per cent.

The company’s US-listed shares fell 7.5 per cent in premarket trading. The market reaction followed the lower growth forecast amid continued weakness in North America and a profit figure below analyst expectations.

AI Revenue Grows Amid Pricing Pressure

AI-related revenue accounted for 10.5 per cent of Infosys’ total revenue in Q2 and grew 29 per cent sequentially, the company said. Chief Executive Officer Salil Parekh said the company was seeing growing demand for AI-related work as enterprises moved towards adoption at scale.

“Worldwide spending on AI services is forecast to reach USD 1.3 trillion by 2030 as enterprise buyers demand efficient, automated service delivery,” said Shubham Singh Rathore, principal analyst at Gartner.

The growth in AI revenue, however, has yet to change the company’s overall revenue outlook. Infosys is navigating a market in which AI is creating new technology-services opportunities while also increasing pressure on traditional work through productivity demands and pricing competition.

For FY27, the company maintained its operating-margin guidance at 20 to 22 per cent while lowering its revenue growth forecast. The pace at which large-deal wins translate into recognised revenue, alongside a recovery in North American demand, will remain important to its growth trajectory.
